Package neqsim.process.diagnostics

Class ValveSeatLeakageAssessment

java.lang.Object
neqsim.process.diagnostics.ValveSeatLeakageAssessment
All Implemented Interfaces:
Serializable
public class ValveSeatLeakageAssessment extends Object implements Serializable
Interprets a field seat-tightness test on a closed isolation valve and turns it into a leak rate, an equivalent leak-gap size, and a screening severity verdict.

Offshore isolation tests report a symptom, not a number: "the cavity went to 4.2 barg in 60 seconds", or "there was still 0.3 barg standing with the bleed fully open". This class converts either observation into kg/s and Sm3/h using real-gas properties from the supplied SystemInterface, and then reports the seat gap that would pass that rate. It answers the question a maintenance engineer actually has - is this seat weepage that sealant injection will cure, or is the seat mechanically damaged?

Two independent test modes are supported, and they deliberately depend on different unknowns, so running both on the same valve is a genuine cross-check rather than a repeat:

  • Pressure build-up - the bleed is shut and the pressure rise in the trapped volume is timed. Needs the trapped volume; does not need the upstream pressure, because the seat gap is choked while the cavity is far below the line pressure.
  • Standing bleed pressure - the bleed is left fully open and the pressure it cannot clear is read. Needs the bleed bore; does not need the trapped volume, because it is a steady state where leak in equals bleed out.

The severity bands are NeqSim screening bands expressed on equivalent gap diameter, not an acceptance criterion from a standard. Acceptance belongs to ValveSeatLeakageClass and to the valve data sheet. 

 ValveSeatLeakageAssessment test = new ValveSeatLeakageAssessment("NP-23-0060", gas);
 test.setTemperature(40.0, "C");
 test.setUpstreamPressure(325.0, "bara");
 test.setPressureBuildUpTest(0.027, 4.2, 60.0);
 ValveSeatLeakageAssessment.Result r = test.calculate();
 r.getLeakRateSm3PerHour();
 r.getEquivalentGapDiameterMm();
 r.getSeverity();
